Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the run chase! The umpires walk back out to the middle as the players of Bangladesh are seen in a huddle before taking their places on the field. No Will Young, so, it will be Rachin Ravindra to open the innings for New Zealand alongside Devon Conway. It will be Mustafizur Rahman to start proceedings off with the new ball here. Let's play...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, Bangladesh do have something to defend but it certainly looks below par and New Zealand will be itching to go on and get their third win of the competition. Also, the head-to-head in World Cups stands 5-0 in favor of the Kiwis, so, Bangladesh will need a performance of a lifetime with the ball and in the field to cause an upset here. Do join us in a few minutes to see how the chase unfolds.

Trent Boult, who brought up 200 ODI wickets in this game is down for a quick chat. Boult talks about the milestone first and says that some will say he is into the stats but confirms that he isn't much into the stats. Adds that you don't play the game for that but it is nice to tick things off like that. Tells that it took him two and a half years to perfect the knuckle ball but it helps when you have bowled around you who can bowl that well. Mentions that the wicket was a bit tougher than expected and reckons 250 was par on this wicket. Ends by saying that Bangladesh batted well but hopes that they can get over the line here.

Bangladesh have got something on the board but it was another inconsistent batting display. Their best batter from the previous game, Litton Das played a very rash shot on the first ball of the game and put his side under pressure right away by throwing his wicket away. Tanzid Hasan and Mehidy Hasan stitched together a decent stand with the latter playing some good shots as well but both got out in a space of less than four overs which meant Bangladesh needed someone to get them out of jail. Mushfiqur Rahim played that role and along with a scratchy Shakib Al Hasan put on a vital 96-run stand. Just as Shakib was getting into a bit of rhythm he too got out but Rahim did go on to score yet another half-century before getting out. There was no upping of the ante or any sort of momentum in the final 10 overs and Mahmudullah who came in at number 8 had to toil long and hard before getting a few big shots away. For the first time in a World Cup game, Bangladesh hit eight maximums but couldn't even get to 250 runs.

End of another fine bowling display from New Zealand but Bangladesh do get 20 runs off the final couple of overs and have limped to 245 runs here. Not the typical Chennai wicket and for a change, it was the pacers who were able to extract some bounce and carry off the deck. A wicket off the very first ball from Trent Boult got the Kiwis going but they had to wait for a bit for the next wicket. It was Lockie Ferguson who peppered the opposition with short balls and picked up a couple of quick wickets. The middle phase was proving to be wicketless for New Zealand but once again Ferguson came in and broke a crucial stand to open the floodgates. From there, the Kiwis kept up the ante and ensured that Bangladesh were restricted to an under-par total. Ferguson ended with 3 with Trent Boult and Matt Henry picking up a couple each and Boult became the third quickest to get to 200 ODI wickets.
A dot to end the innings then! Daryl Mitchell serves this full and outside off, angling away, Shoriful Islam looks to slog it away but only connects with thin air. Bangladesh finishes on 245/9!

Litton Das looks to be aggressive and put Boult under pressure by stepping out and decides to whip it away off his hips. Commentary.Commentary: Done with the pre-match formalities! We can see the New Zealand players in a huddle and now they spread out to take their respective field positions. Litton Das and Tanzid Hasan are the two openers for Bangladesh. Trent Boult has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...

We are moments away from the start of the game but before that, the players from both sides line up for their respective national anthems. It will be Bangladesh's first followed by the national anthem of New Zealand.

Bangladesh (Playing XI) - Litton Das, Tanzid Hasan, Najmul Hossain Shanto, Shakib Al Hasan (C), Mehidy Hasan, Mushfiqur Rahim (WK), Towhid Hridoy, Mahmudullah (In place of Mahedi Hasan), Taskin Ahmed, Mustafizur Rahman, Shoriful Islam.

New Zealand (Playing XI) - Devon Conway, Rachin Ravindra, Kane Williamson (C) (In place of Will Young), Daryl Mitchell, Tom Latham (WK), Glenn Phillips, Mark Chapman, Mitchell Santner, Matt Henry, Lockie Ferguson, Trent Boult.

Shakib Al Hasan, captain of Bangladesh says that he was a bit confused but don't mind batting first. Adds that the pitch looks good and the ball would come on nicely onto the bat. Tells that you win some, you lose some but it is important to how you come back and play well. Mentions they did no start well with the bat nor with the ball against England and need to be better in the Powerplay. Informs Mahmudullah replaces Mahedi Hasan.

Kane Williamson, the captain of New Zealand says that they will have a bowl first with potential dew in the evening. Adds that he was able to take part in the warm-up games and is happy to be back in the team. Mentions that there have been a number of positives and ends by informing that he replaces Will Young in the side.
TOSS - The coin lands in favour of Kane Williamson and New Zealand have elected to BOWL first.

PITCH REPORT - Michael Atherton is pitchside and says that the pitch is a bit off-center and the short boundary on one side is just 59 meters with the straight boundary being 76 meters. Sanjay Manjrekar joins him and says that the pitch looks like a stark contrast to the one in the India-Australia game and it is a much better batting surface. Reckons that Bangladesh might have enjoyed more of a turning wicket against the Kiwis but will be happy.
UPDATE - Huge news coming from the Kiwis camp as Kane Williamson is all set to make his return in this game and will lead the side.

Bangladesh have been fairly hard to beat in home conditions in bilaterals in the last few years and will feel the surface they are playing on in this game is quite close to what they would get back home. They do have a win under their belt but are also coming into this game on the back of a thrashing. The bowling has enough depth in it to trouble any opposition and it's all about the application with the bat and that has been lacking. Will we witness Bangladesh notch up a huge win? Or will the Kiwis make it three wins out of three? We shall find out in due course. Toss and team news in a bit.

New Zealand have started their campaign with a couple of fairly straightforward wins and look like a well-drilled side as they always do in big events. The top order is firing and a couple of bowlers are in really good form. They do have a couple of headaches as both Kane Williamson and Tim Southee might be available for this clash and if they do tinker with the playing XI, who will come in and who will be benched? We'll have to keep a close eye on that.

Hello and a warm welcome to Match number 11 of the 2023 Cricket World Cup where New Zealand will be taking on Bangladesh in a crucial clash at the Chepauk Stadium in hot and humid Chennai. Two teams who will enjoy playing on this surface given one team's prowess against spin and the other team being filled with spinners and it should be an entertaining clash.

The 2023 ICC Cricket World Cup caravan is back in Chennai for Match number 11 of this long tournament where high-flying New Zealand will meet an inconsistent Bangladesh side at the M.A. Chidambaram Stadium in a big clash. The Kiwis have started the tournament with a couple of astounding victories and have hardly broken a sweat in doing so. After thrashing reigning champions England, New Zealand made lightwork of the Netherlands to zoom to the top of the table. Their top order remained in fantastic form as an under-par Will Young too managed to have a solid outing. The middle order did see a couple of batters mustering valuable runs but will look to plug a few small holes that were visible in the latter half of their innings. With the likes of Kane Williamson and Tim Southee expected to be fit for this clash, the coaching staff have a real headache if they want to tinker with the playing XI or not. Moving to their bowling, a couple of names are a no-brainer with Mitchell Santner and Matt Henry proving to be really consistent and their wicket-taking ability gives them that X-factor. Trent Boult has been a shade under his best and Lockie Ferguson who did feature in the previous game wasn't at his best either. This opens up the door for Tim Southee or even Ish Sodhi given the nature of the track in Chennai to make the cut. Bangladesh on the other end were on the receiving end of England's wrath in the previous game and it was their batting that was a big question mark even though they conceded 350+ runs. The top order needs to fire and the likes of Tanzid Hasan and Najmul Hossain Shanto need their form leading up to the tournament to really shine at the big stage. The middle order does have some experienced names but Towhid Hridoy seems like the most consistent batter. The form of Mustafizur Rahman has been a sign of worry in recent times but Shoriful Islam on the other hand is only getting better. They do have a plethora of spinners and will look to make the most out of the spin-friendly conditions in Chennai to cause an upset. Can the Bangla Tigers roar and win big? Or will the Black Caps continue on their merry way? We shall find out.
